parsedVerdict.reasoning: The application module serves one concern: the order and stock use cases. The not-found check is written once, in OrderLookupService.require, and all single-order use cases (Advance, Cancel, Get) call it rather than calling the repository's findById themselves. DTO mapping is written once in DtoMapper (toOrderDto, toProductStockDto) and every use case that returns a DTO uses it. Time and IDs come from the Clock and IdGenerator ports. dto.ts and errors.ts hold the shared data shapes and error types. Stock handling is split by use case into reserve, release and dispatch, which are different operations and not copies of one rule. State-change rules stay in the domain (order.advanceTo, order.cancel). ListOrdersUseCase reads the repository directly for list queries, which doesn't go around the lookup service, because that service only covers fetching one order that must exist. ValidationError is unused inside the module, probably because infrastructure's requestParsers uses it; this is not a split.
